what: The qc judge gets its own row and role file (agents/qc-judge.md); the code reviewer is no longer run headless for just qc, judges code quality only, reads pstack interrogate's code-quality review and lead-judgment references, and blocks only on a documented standards breach or a named simplification listing the lines it deletes.
why: Owner ruling, issue #67 items 1 and 2: on #51 the reviewer built hostile setups from its 'run the changed behavior' line and the patch's broken-behaviour block; only 1 of 6 blocks traced to the spec. Fix by deleting those instructions.
evidence: Two contradicting lines once this PR lands: agents/code-reviewer.md and .skillfile/patches/skills/code-review (issue #67 items 2 and 4 delete the Spec axis and the broken-behaviour block) against roles#roles-reviewer-patch 'it blocks only on a failed acceptance criterion, broken behavior or a hard standard' and #role-code-reviewer 'headless for each just qc run'.

what: The lane key names workspace, branch, lane record and agent names: gh<N> for GitHub, the lowercased Linear key (eng-123) for Linear; a recipe's N is the parent ticket as the tracker writes it; a role's skills line may name {tracker}, which pi-role resolves from .octo-feather.toml. Adds acceptance-supervise-layout-linear.
why: Owner ruling (2026-10-22, issue #82): the kit works with Linear directly so it can run on a Linear-first repository; the tracker is set per target in .octo-feather.toml, tracker work lives in packaged skills (github-pr, github-issues, linear) behind fixed script names, and ADR 0004 and 0011 were corrected in place to match.
evidence: Corrected ADR 0004 says the tracker is GitHub Issues or Linear, chosen per target, and ADR 0011 that a Linear lane's key is its lowercased ticket key, while the spec as accepted says 'tab supervisor in workspace gh<N>' (role-supervisor); the accepted criteria cannot pass on a Linear target.
